content: Ezetimibe is a medication prescribed to help lower cholesterol and other fatty substances in the blood. It is typically used alongside lifestyle changes, such as following a healthy diet, losing weight, and exercising regularly. This medication can be taken on its own or in combination with a statin (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor). Ezetimibe belongs to a class of drugs known as cholesterol-lowering medications and works by reducing the absorption of cholesterol in the intestines. By lowering cholesterol and fat levels in the blood, it can help reduce the risk of developing heart disease, angina (chest pain), strokes, and heart attacks. Ezetimibe is available in tablet form and is usually taken once daily, with or without food. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not take more or less of the medication than prescribed, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor, even if you feel well. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes. If you have questions about additional uses, ask your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before starting ezetimibe, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Certain medications, such as anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), cyclosporine, fenofibrate, and gemfibrozil, may require dose adjustments or careful monitoring for side effects. If you are taking bile acid sequestrants like cholestyramine, colesevelam, or colestipol, take them either four hours before or two hours after ezetimibe. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have a history of liver disease, are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking ezetimibe, contact your doctor immediately. While taking ezetimibe, it is important to follow a low-cholesterol, low-fat diet. This includes foods like fat-free milk, cottage cheese, fish (not canned in oil), vegetables, poultry, egg whites, and polyunsaturated oils (e.g., corn, safflower, canola, soybean). Avoid high-fat foods such as fatty meats, liver, egg yolks, whole milk, cream, butter, lard, pastries, fried foods, and oils like coconut or palm oil. If you miss a dose of ezetimibe, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Ezetimibe may cause side effects. Minor side effects include headache, dizziness, diarrhea, sore throat, runny nose, sneezing, and joint pain. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, though rare, require immediate medical attention. These include hives, rash, itching, difficulty breathing or swallowing, swelling of the face or extremities, hoarseness, severe fatigue, unusual bleeding or bruising, loss of appetite, yellowing of the skin or eyes, flu-like symptoms, muscle pain or weakness, chest pain, or pale or fatty stools. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor promptly. Store ezetimibe in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments while taking ezetimibe. Your doctor will monitor your response to the medication through regular lab tests. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Ezetimibe is available under the brand names Zetia® and Vytorin® (when combined with simvastatin).
